Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Sam, the dog detective (a big brown dog in a light blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped dark blue tie and a blue-gray fedora). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: animation 8, facing right (8 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 400 to 448 pixels tall and from 276 to 312 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig209_03/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.


SCOPED SOURCE CORRECTION. Generate ONLY the 6 source composite sprites shown in the FIRST reference image, in the same 3-column 2-row grid, keep unused slots empty. Output 1536x1024 transparent RGBA. This is an intermediate production component sheet, not the final atlas. Each sprite includes BOTH the glass chamber AND the characters shown inside it. The chamber is a blue/lavender and white glass apparatus with thin orange side edges and tiny gray projections below. Keep its exact asymmetric outline, reflections, blue fill and overlaid glass panels. The characters are deliberately UPSIDE DOWN: Sam's feet at top, dog muzzle and fedora at bottom. DO NOT rotate, mirror or normalize them. Sam has brown dog fur, bare paws, blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped navy/black tie. Some later source sprites ALSO contain cream-white MAX, with warm beige shadows, elongated ears and teeth. Preserve his source-specific inverted/turning posture and warm palette, never replace with generic standing white Max. The two master sheets are ONLY identity and ink style anchors. The original FIRST source controls every pose, proportions, hand overlap and color. Keep the chamber consistent across cels. Source blue/lavender glass overlays ARE artwork, not transparent padding: preserve their tint over the figures where shown; do not put this overlay on poses where absent. Exterior magenta and gray alone become fully transparent. No floor shadows, no text, no labels, no glow, no extra mechanisms. Clean hand ink, flat colors with one shade, restrained highlights. Repaint the original clusters faithfully without enlarging heads or changing finger/foot/ear locations. Preserve all original partial forms. We will scale/place whole NEW composite sprites to exact original boxes without original masks or warping.
Tiny source detail: sprite cel1941 (bottom middle) has an isolated pale blue-gray fleck to its left, separate from the chamber. Preserve it as a separate tiny mark, do not stretch the chamber toward it. The tiny underside gray strokes belong to the apparatus and must remain in every sprite.
CRITICAL ANATOMY CORRECTION FROM SOURCE: In the FIRST FIVE sprites Max is SEEN FROM BEHIND and is upside down relative to the frame. At the TOP are two flat outward-pointing FEET, then thin LEGS, then his small lower torso with a round TAIL. The large cream oval below is the BACK OF HIS HEAD. The two long lobes hanging DOWN toward Sam's face are MAX'S EARS, NOT LEGS. Small arms extend beside his lower torso. Absolutely NO FACE, eyes, nose or teeth on those first five rear-view Max sprites. Sam grips the hanging ears as shown. In sprite SIX, Max has been turned: his ears now extend upward, his face is visible, feet lower. The source anatomy must be copied exactly even though unconventional. Do not invent facial features on the tail/buttocks. In first five keep back of head as one plain oval. This correction supersedes generic standing-Max expectations.
